feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications/strategy and credible progression at NACo. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression: the NACo trajectory shows increasing scope, leadership, and ownership, which strengthens credibility.  
- Good strategic/technical balance: combines communications leadership with CMS, analytics, and workflow modernization expertise.  
- Writing is polished and readable: tone is professional, concise, and tailored to mission-driven/public-sector environments.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include metrics on growth, engagement, efficiency, campaign performance, cost savings, or team impact where possible.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation around list bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma in one role; “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” or “Elementary (A2).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding mission-driven digital leadership will make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with current value proposition: digital strategy leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a more concise grouping to improve flow.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable complex teams to operate effectively. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “workflows and systems” overlap with Core Competencies; keep the intro high-level.
- “Advocacy messaging” is reinforced throughout NACo roles, so avoid adding more detail here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It will be more effective if tightened to emphasize senior-level strengths and reduce generic phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, higher-value language: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & insight reporting.”
- Group related items and remove filler like “multi-channel communication,” which is already covered elsewhere.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial workflow design & governance • Cross-channel content strategy • Analytics, dashboards & performance reporting • Stakeholder and cross-functional leadership • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia, livestream and event production
- Keep style consistent: use either “and” or “&” throughout; “cross-functional” reads more naturally than “cross-department.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat language already stated in the summary and Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list rather than a high-impact recent engagement. Tighten it around 3–4 signature contributions and add scale, outputs, or outcomes where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, web modernization and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Built cross-channel workflows, governance standards and analytics systems to improve coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-driven: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components and downloadable member toolkits.” Add metrics if available.
- Sharpen the AI/search bullet: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows and user discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording overlaps with header/core competencies and NACo bullets on governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement.
- Footer project examples already cover microsites and AI search; avoid repeating the same detail here unless you add outcomes.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in the earlier NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive wins first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email/social growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign impact if available.
- Condense into 4–5 bullets, e.g.:
- Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting and decision support.
- Launched NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding advocacy, event, and recurring content production.
- Established stronger digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-program language also overlaps with the footer projects and earlier NACo roles.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution-level leadership and channel growth, not broad digital oversight.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy content delivery.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scale/results: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with concrete operational impact: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/publishing standards; keep this at the process-building level.
- Weekly video/livestream language also appears in the earlier NACo role; frame this here as scaling an established format rather than originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the leadership scope and emphasize the most recent, higher-value strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “AI-enabled content discovery” if you want stronger alignment with recent consulting work.
- Keep terms that reflect leadership and systems ownership, not just messaging.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is weaker than the CV’s stronger recurring framing around communications operations, governance, and platform leadership.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it currently reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and platform delivery rather than listing every platform/language.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Consider replacing “Power Pages” and/or “SharePoint” with a broader phrase like “enterprise web platforms” if those tools are not prominent in recent experience.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to echo the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section duplicates the “Technical + IT” inventory; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave detailed tools to Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the exact phrase verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools here and move the full stack detail to Technical + IT.
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity; KPI design, executive reporting, SEO and digital performance analysis.”
- If accurate, strengthen with scope language tied to recent work: “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “organization-wide reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; avoid repeating the exact same tool list in both places.
- “Leadership reporting” may be stronger as “executive reporting” for clarity and seniority.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple work bullets. Make it tighter, more senior, and oriented to delivery capability rather than listing tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Replace with concise, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- PTZ camera, studio and control-room operations
- Virtual event production and speaker/run-of-show coordination
- If space allows, swap one tool-based bullet for an outcome-oriented phrase: **In-house studio and recurring advocacy video production**
- Keep wording parallel and avoid mixing broad functions with specific equipment unless the equipment is a hiring keyword.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” substantially duplicate the Core Competencies line on multimedia/livestream operations.
- “Studio operations” and PTZ systems are already supported by the NACo Director role; don’t overstate them here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills almost exactly. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/current platforms or broadened with context that adds value.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current, proven platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” if brief descriptors are allowed.
- If space is tight, drop the weakest/least evidenced tool: GitHub Pages appears least supported by the experience bullets.
- Consider renaming to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, align ordering to recency/strength: Drupal first by a wide margin, then WordPress/SharePoint.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is redundant with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- Avoid repeating platform names in both sections unless one is repositioned as a shorter “tools” list and the other adds context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and slightly more current/senior.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from languages/tools to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “Drupal front-end implementation” or “technical troubleshooting for public-facing web platforms.”
- Order by relevance/modernity: JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, Google Tag Manager, HTML/CSS, jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing.
- GTM may also fit under analytics/optimization if you need to tighten this section.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Make it more selective and signal how these tools were used in recent leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for clarity: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to use: “Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project tracking), Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)”
- Consider trimming to the strongest, most relevant tools from recent roles; if you didn’t use all of Basecamp/Trello/Jira recently, remove older/secondary platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support an operations/workflow narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it’s too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership implied by recent email leadership. Tighten naming and, if possible, signal enterprise-level use rather than just listing tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename for clarity and seniority: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Standardize product names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to show level of use, e.g. **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (enterprise campaign automation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications/community)** • **Mailchimp (newsletter and campaign sends)**
- If one platform was primary in the 2022–2024 role, place it first to reflect recency and strongest relevance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters; keep this section tool-focused and avoid repeating audience-size metrics here.
- “Engagement” may overlap with core competency language on multi-channel communications; use platform-specific wording instead.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it read as the foundational build phase: team formation, early platform/process improvements, and first recurring multimedia outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize setup/build work: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and scope: “Supported a major website refresh, coordinated digital publishing operations, and produced recurring multimedia content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Tighten the management point: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped supervise a digital media associate.”
- If available, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; distinguish this as launching/producing the early version.
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social, video” leadership language already used more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the most distinctive achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten wording: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Remove vague phrasing like “organizational programs and policy work” and “contributed to”; use stronger verbs such as coordinated, translated, launched, produced.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience growth, or types/volume of projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content production; later roles already cover web, video, newsletters and multimedia leadership in more depth.
- Don’t repeat “first podcast” elsewhere unless it is a major cross-role achievement.
